sentences.text: Liaoningotitan was a medium-sized sauropod that grew to about 10 meters long with a shoulder height of 2 meters.
This dinosaur is distinguished by a convex ventral margin of the maxilla and a short, anteriorly positioned upper tooth row.
Its lower jaw held nine reduced, un-imbricated teeth with asymmetric, elliptical-like crowns featuring lingual grooves, ridges, and a bulbous basal crown.
Zhou et al. (2018) classified Liaoningotitan as a somphospondylan titanosauriform that is more derived than Euhelopus.
A redescription of the holotype specimen — the specimen the species is based on — proposed that Liaoningotitan is affiliated with the family Euhelopodidae.
Liaoningotitan lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
In a 2025 redescription, Bingqing Shan proposed that Liaoningotitan belongs to the Euhelopodidae family as the sister taxon to Yongjinglong.
